# What Databricks personal access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves
# alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is: a body is thirty-two hexadecimal characters, so the run twice
# over is one, and the prefix in front brings a token to thirty-six. Where a case
# turns on what a body may close on, it closes one on da or on d instead. The
# hyphen and digit some tokens carry bring one to thirty-eight.

patterns: databricks-personal-access-token

# The one prefix Databricks writes a token with. There is a single kind of string
# here rather than a table of them: the token a workspace user creates and the
# token a service principal is issued are the same string with no mark on it to
# tell one from another, so the cases below are that one shape in the places a
# token is written.

case:     a token in an environment assignment
in:       DATABRICKS_TOKEN=dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DATABRICKS_TOKEN=«databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in the profile the cli writes
in:       [DEFAULT]\nhost = https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com\ntoken = dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      [DEFAULT]\nhost = https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com\ntoken = «databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in the header a request carries it in
in:       Authorization: Bearer dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: Bearer «databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in the property a jdbc connection takes it as
in:       jdbc:databricks://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com:443/default;PWD=dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      jdbc:databricks://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com:443/default;PWD=«databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a token in the json the token endpoint returns
in:       {"token_value":"dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      {"token_value":"«databricks-personal-access-token»"}

# The hyphen and the digit some tokens carry. No Databricks document writes them
# down, and the pattern's own file says what is read there and why; what the
# cases show is that one digit is read and no more, so a longer number written
# behind a token is a tail and what follows it, exactly as a longer run of the
# body alphabet is a body and what follows it.

case:     a token carrying the tail
in:       DATABRICKS_TOKEN=dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-2
out:      DATABRICKS_TOKEN=«databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a hyphen with no digit behind it is no tail
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»-

case:     a hyphen with a letter behind it is no tail
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-a
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»-a

case:     a number longer than one digit is a tail and what follows it
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-2026-01-01
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»026-01-01

# The alphabet the thirty-two characters are written in: lowercase hexadecimal,
# which is what the rulesets that read this format agree on and what a
# hexadecimal encoder settles once for all of its output. Uppercase is the
# widening the pattern's own file declines, and a body carrying anything else is
# no body at all.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       dapi0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      dapi0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF

case:     one uppercase character in a body
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeF
out:      dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdeF

case:     a body carrying a letter outside hexadecimal
in:       dapi0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef
out:      dapi0123456789abcdefg123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef
out:      dapi0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef

# The lengths either side of thirty-two. That count is the 128-bit key
# Databricks' own classifier names, and it is used as a count rather than a
# floor: thirty-one characters are not a token, and thirty-three are a token and
# one character that belongs to no credential. The second of those is the price
# of having no boundary behind the match — a boundary there would drop this token
# rather than trim it, and a real token written against a letter would come
# through whole.

case:     a body of thirty-two characters is a token
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a body of thirty-one characters is not
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     an alphabet run longer than a token is a token and what follows it
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»0

# What a token may be written against. The prefix is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a token keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       DATABRICKS_TOKEN_dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DATABRICKS_TOKEN_«databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xdapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the token is «databricks-personal-access-token».

# Two tokens written together. A token can begin inside another, and the p of the
# prefix is what bounds where: a candidate is found at that character and read
# back two places from it, and the only p a token holds is the one its own prefix
# carries, so a token beginning inside another begins at the last two characters
# of the body, with that p standing past the end of the span. The two spans
# overlap there and are redacted as one. Written without that overlap the two are
# separate values and both go, and a prefix standing where a body would have to
# hold it ends the candidate in front of it and opens the token itself.

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefdapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»«databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a token beginning two characters from the end of the token before it
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcddapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a token beginning at the last character of the token before it
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdedapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     a prefix written where a body would stand
in:       dapi0123456789abcdapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      dapi0123456789abc«databricks-personal-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. Thirty-two lowercase hexadecimal
# characters behind the prefix is the vendor's format exactly, and an MD5 is
# thirty-two of them, so the prefix written straight in front of one is a token
# character for character and the whole of it goes. A longer digest is redacted
# for thirty-six characters with the rest left in the text. That is the answer
# rather than a fault in it, because nothing in the text tells such a run from a
# token: sparing these would spare a real token written the same way. What is
# taken is a stretch of a value that was already opaque.

case:     the prefix in front of an md5
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-1
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»01234567

case:     the prefix in front of a sha-256
in:       dapi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «databricks-personal-access-token»0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what this pattern leaves alone. The first two are the prefix, which is read
# in the case Databricks writes it and with every character of it; the third is a
# UUID, whose hyphens are no character a body may hold, so a hexadecimal run
# divided that way is no body however many characters it comes to. Then a word
# written against the prefix, whose body runs out at the first character
# hexadecimal has not got. The last three carry no prefix at all: a hexadecimal
# run holds neither the p nor the i, so no digest carries one partway along.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       DAPI0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DAPI0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix without its closing letter
in:       dap0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01
out:      dap0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01

case:     a uuid behind the prefix
in:       dapi01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      dapi01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a word written against the prefix
in:       dapideadbeefcafe is no token
out:      dapideadbeefcafe is no token

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      xxxx0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a digest with no prefix
in:       md5=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      md5=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

# And another credential Databricks issues a service principal, which this
# pattern has nothing to say about. An OAuth client secret is written dose and a
# body of a different alphabet, and carries no dapi to be found at; it is a
# credential this pattern's name does not cover rather than one the scan happens
# to miss.

case:     an oauth client secret
in:       DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET=dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET=dose0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a log line naming the api a token authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com/api/2.0/clusters/list
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="calling api" url=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com/api/2.0/clusters/list

case:     the workspace host a token authenticates against
in:       DATABRICKS_HOST=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com
out:      DATABRICKS_HOST=https://dbc-01234567-89ab.cloud.databricks.com
